skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code spans, not executable Ruby or shell backticks. Two git command instructions are confirmed as medium-risk because they combine external commands with a user-supplied fixed point and should require argument-safe execution.

remediation.issue: Git commands include a user-supplied fixed point.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to validate the ref with git rev-parse and pass it as a separate argument, never through shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The skill does not warn against command separators in the fixed point.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to reject refs containing whitespace, shell metacharacters, or option-like values before running git commands.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes Against Standards and Specs
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss whether a change follows local standards or actually satisfies the request. This skill separates both checks and returns focused findings for each axis.
actual_capabilities: Reviews changes between HEAD and a user-provided git fixed point.
Separates standards compliance findings from spec compliance findings.
Uses repository documentation and a fixed code smell baseline.
Looks for related issues, PRD files, or spec files before spec review.
Aggregates parallel sub-agent reports without merging their priorities.
limitations: Requires a valid git fixed point, such as a branch, tag, or commit.
Spec review is skipped when no issue, PRD, or spec source is available.
Findings are heuristic and should be checked against project context.
The workflow depends on the host agent supporting parallel sub-agents.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Review a branch before merge and separate convention issues from missed product requirements.

use_cases.title: Spec Compliance Check
use_cases.description: Compare implemented behavior against an issue, PRD, or feature specification before handoff.

use_cases.title: Repository Standards Audit
use_cases.description: Check whether a work-in-progress change follows local standards and common maintainability heuristics.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current branch since main.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review against the default integration branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review Since Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changes since commit abc123 against our standards and the linked issue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Target a specific fixed point for a focused review.

prompt_templates.title: Review With Spec Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since origin/main and use docs/specs/billing-redesign.md as the spec source.
prompt_templates.scenario: Provide an explicit specification document when issue discovery is not enough.

prompt_templates.title: Review Release Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review release/payment-v2 since v1.8.0 and keep standards findings separate from spec findings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a larger branch or release candidate.

output_examples.input: Review since main for a feature branch with a linked issue.
output_examples.output: The report contains a Standards section with convention and smell findings, then a Spec section with missing or extra behavior.

output_examples.input: Review since origin/main with no available spec.
output_examples.output: The report includes standards findings and clearly states that the spec axis was skipped because no spec source was found.

output_examples.input: Review since a release tag with a PRD file path.
output_examples.output: The report cites PRD requirements separately from code standard concerns and ends with per-axis counts.

best_practices: Provide an explicit fixed point, such as main, a tag, or a commit SHA.
Point the skill to the relevant issue, PRD, or spec when discovery may be ambiguous.
Review each axis separately before deciding what must block a merge.
anti_patterns: Do not use the review as a replacement for tests, type checks, or security scanning.
Do not treat code smell findings as hard failures without project context.
Do not run git commands with untrusted refs through shell interpolation.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews a git diff against repository standards and against the intended specification.

faq.question: Does it need a fixed point?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a branch, tag, commit, or merge-base reference for comparison.

faq.question: What happens if no spec exists?
faq.answer: The skill skips the Spec axis and reports that no spec source was available.

faq.question: Can it find code smells?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a fixed baseline of maintainability smells when project standards are incomplete.

faq.question: Does it merge all findings into one priority list?
faq.answer: No. It keeps Standards and Spec results separate so one axis does not hide the other.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
